episode.title: Venus: A Day Longer Than Its Year

synopsis: This episode illustrates Venus's incredibly slow rotation, resulting in a day longer than its orbital year.
narration: On Venus, a single day stretches longer than its entire orbital year. This slow rotation, combined with its rapid orbit, creates a unique temporal paradox. Experience the sun crawling across a scorching, toxic sky. Time itself moves differently on this infernal world.

shots.prompt: Venus, a dominant, hazy yellow-orange sphere, slowly rotating against a backdrop of distant, pinprick stars. The atmosphere is thick and opaque, obscuring the surface. Camera slowly tracks the planet's rotation, emphasizing its sluggishness.

Time-lapse effect on the Venusian horizon. A colossal, distorted sun slowly creeps across the sky, casting long, shifting shadows across a desolate, reddish-brown landscape, hinting at the scorching surface beneath thick clouds. The sun's movement is almost imperceptible.

Pull back to a wide shot of Venus as a full disk, now showing its rapid orbital path around a distant, bright sun. The planet itself rotates at an almost imperceptible pace, contrasting its swift journey through space with its internal temporal scale. Gently loops back to shot 1's composition.

music: An awe-driven cosmic underscore with a slow, heavy, atmospheric pulse, building with a subtle, sustained chord for the scale moment, emphasizing the immense duration. The music should evoke a sense of deep time and oppressive gravity, ending mid-phrase for seamless looping.
